newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee seen in band before next move.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee seen in band before next move.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40

LIFFE coffee futures have probably seen the best of gains and the worst of falls and the prices are now locked in a wide $1,788-$2,000 band basis September before the next decisive move, technical analysts said on Thursday.
The market was due $75 down after heavy losses in New York on Wednesday on forecasts of a warmer temperature in Brazil's coffee belt.
On the New York market, September's fall to below $1.85 per lb triggered heavy speculative stop-loss selling.
"On a technical perspective it looks as if prices are going all the way back to $1.51," broker GNI said in a commentary.
September finished almost at the day's floor of 175.50 for a hefty 15.15 cent loss and the lowest level since April 22.
Some industry sources said the downturn was heightened by liquidation pressure on the spot contract ahead of July's month-long delivery period on Friday.
Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst, said coffee had had a very reasonable rally and probably seen the best of gains.
London's September faced a critical resistance at $2,000, a level not seen since June 10.
"But the market has also seen the lows," she said. "If it holds above $1,778, then I'm pretty sure of that."
Since rallying to a peak of $2,700 on May 29, the robusta market has fallen to a low of $1,695 on June 11 before rebounding to a high of $1,975 on Wednesday.
